newsitem.title: USA: VOA to broadcast B-92 reports to Serbia.
newsitem.headline: VOA to broadcast B-92 reports to Serbia.

text.p: In response to Serbia's closedown of independent Radio B-92, the U.S. government's Voice of America will broadcast reports from the radio's correspondents into Serbia starting on Wednesday, VOA said.

The U.S. broadcaster said in a statement it was expanding its medium- and short-wave Serbian-language transmissions from two to two-and-a-half hours daily to accommodate reports by B-92 journalists and interviews with them.

The move would "provide a special daily window of events to the people of Serbia in their own language, easily accessible on car radios and the standard broadcast band," said VOA South European Division Chief Frank Shkreli.

He described it as "fully consistent with the Voice's tradition of including a rich mix of accurate local, regional and U.S. news at a time when the free flow of information in a particular country is threatened".
Serbian authorities closed down B-92 on Tuesday as demonstrations continued in Belgrade over what opposition parties said was massive fraud by the ruling socialists in local elections last month.
The authorities said the station, one of the few independent news sources in Serbia, was operating without a license.

The United States condemned the shutdown as "a transparent effort to keep the Serbian public in the dark" and said it demonstrated "the fundamental lack of respect ... the Serbian government has for democratic principles."
VOA, the international radio service of the U.S. Information Agency, broadcasts in 52 languages and claims 86 million listeners per week worldwide.
